newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Oct 4.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Oct 4.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stockmarkets on Friday morning.
NEWS OUTLOOK:

** The Congress party's crucial support for the ruling minority coalition depended on reciprocal backing for Congress in India's most populous state of Uttar Pradesh where local elections are underway, its chief says
** Global investment bank Merrill Lynch hails India's economic reforms as one of the most successful among emerging markets, says country's outlook was positive
** Aluminiums hit a fresh 2-1/4 year low and copper failed to hold above the $1,900 level as the London Metal Exchange (LME) closed weakly on Thursday
Three months aluminium dived to a fresh 2-1/4 year low
of $1,340 early on the LME but clawed its way up to close at $1,352, a $25 loss from Wednesday, on trade buying, mostly from the Far East
** India's export growth rate during April-August declined sharply to 9.8 percent compared with same period last year, the Business Standard reports

** The International Monetary Fund will help countries crack down on money laundering, which it said could undermine their financial stability, the Fund's managing director Michel Camdessus said on Thursday
** The spot dollar/rupee opened steady at 35.62/64 per dollar , dealers said
MARKETS:
** On Thursday, shares across India drifted lower in dull listless trade with action limited to few pivotals
** The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index dropped 31.03 points, or 0.96 percent, to 3,195.77
** The 100-share National index eased 7.57 points, or 0.52 percent, to 1,439.86
** The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index slipped 11.35 points, of 1.21 percent, to 921.18
** The 500-share CRISIL index was off 6.80 points, or 1.09 percent, at 616.64
** The Delhi share index dropped 3.75 points to 715.99
** The Calcutta index shed 1.84 points to 421.54
** The Madras index fell 28.51 points to 3,344.76
** The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR Index slipped 0.31 points, or 0.48 percent, to 64.69 with the premium over the local market at 9.39 percent against Wednesday's 8.49 percent
